learning_objective: 🎯 Explore the foundation of geometry! Learn how intersecting lines create angles, and uncover the magical relationships between them.

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Angles are measured in degrees. An 'Acute' angle is less than 90°. A 'Right' angle is exactly 90°. An 'Obtuse' angle is between 90° and 180°. A 'Straight' angle is exactly 180°, forming a flat line.

Two angles are 'Complementary' if they add up to 90°. They are 'Supplementary' if they add up to 180°. If two lines cross in an 'X' shape, the opposite angles ('Vertically Opposite Angles') are always perfectly equal!
When a straight line (Transversal) slices through two parallel lines, it creates 8 angles. A beautiful symmetry occurs: Alternate Interior angles are equal, and Corresponding angles are equal.

fun_activity.title: ⏰ The Clock Angle Master
fun_activity.instructions: Look at an analog clock. At exactly 3:00, the hands make a 90° (Right) angle. At 6:00, they make a 180° (Straight) angle. What kind of angle do the hands make at 2:00? (Hint: The whole circle is 360° divided by 12 hours!)

exam_tips: 📌 The 'Linear Pair Axiom' is crucial: If a ray stands on a line, the sum of the two adjacent angles formed is 180°.
📌 If a transversal cuts two lines and makes the alternate interior angles EQUAL, then those two lines MUST be parallel. This works both ways!
📌 Sum of angles around a single point is always exactly 360°.
quick_recap: ⭐ Angles are formed when two rays originate from the same endpoint.
⭐ Vertically opposite angles formed by intersecting lines are always equal.
⭐ A transversal cutting parallel lines creates equal corresponding and alternate interior angles.
